channel.title: US Visa Policy (English)
channel.description: USCIS and State Department policy updates in five languages

item.title: CBP Proposes Mandatory Advance Traveler Information for Rail Crossings
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has proposed requiring rail carriers to transmit advance electronic traveler information to CBP for all passengers and crew arriving in or departing from the United States by train. The rule, which also requires advance notice of arrival or departure, is not yet final and CBP is accepting comments until December 14, 2026.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Illegal Aliens Convicted of Murder, Child Abuse, Rape
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested several illegal aliens with criminal convictions for murder, child sexual abuse, vehicular homicide, and rape. DHS said the arrests are part of ongoing efforts under the Trump administration to remove criminal aliens from communities.

item.title: Cuban Lawful Permanent Resident Arrested for Unlawfully Voting in Missouri
item.description: A 64-year-old Cuban national and lawful permanent resident, Andres Garcia, was arrested in Kansas City, Missouri, after being charged with illegally voting in the 2022 and 2024 federal elections. USCIS assisted in the investigation led by ICE Homeland Security Investigations, and the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri is prosecuting the case.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Criminal Histories of Illegal Aliens Arrested in Syracuse, NY
item.description: DHS released a statement listing illegal aliens arrested by ICE in Syracuse, New York, citing criminal histories including sexual exploitation of a minor, sexual assault, cocaine possession, DUI, and burglary. The release quotes DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin pledging continued enforcement despite New York sanctuary policies.

item.title: DHS Disputes NYC Mayor's Account of ICE Shooting, Cites Nearly 15,000 Unhonored Detainers
item.description: DHS issued a statement responding to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's comments on an October 8 incident in which an ICE officer discharged a weapon during an attempted arrest in the Bronx. DHS disputed several of the mayor's claims and said New York has failed to honor nearly 15,000 ICE detainers since January 2025.

item.title: DHS Announces Deportation of Criminal Aliens with Gang Ties, Including Violent Offenders
item.description: DHS reported that ICE deported several illegal aliens with gang affiliations in the past week, including individuals convicted of attempted murder, aggravated assault, robbery and driving under the influence. The release lists each individual's criminal history and immigration background.

item.title: DHS and EOIR finalize rule on civil penalties for failure to depart and illegal entry
item.description: DHS and the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) have issued a final rule finalizing their June 2025 interim final rule on civil monetary penalties for certain immigration violations. The final rule keeps the prior procedures largely unchanged but adds one new provision allowing late-filed appeals in cases of documented mail delivery delays beyond the alien's control.

item.title: USCIS Opens New Asylum Office in Charlotte, North Carolina
item.description: USCIS is opening a new asylum office in Charlotte, North Carolina. Starting October 13, 2026, asylum applicants residing in North Carolina or South Carolina will fall under this office's jurisdiction and may be scheduled for interviews there.

item.title: Former Medical Doctor Convicted of Naturalization Fraud in Ohio
item.description: USCIS said it provided critical assistance in an investigation that led to the conviction of former internal medicine doctor Yousif Abdulraouf Alhallaq for naturalization fraud. He lied on his Form N-400 and in a sworn interview about a 2014 attack on his pregnant girlfriend before becoming a U.S. citizen in 2018.

item.title: Homeland Security Task Force Probe Leads to 20-Year Sentence for Illegal Alien Drug Trafficker
item.description: DHS announced that a Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) investigation led by ICE's Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) resulted in a 20-year prison sentence for Jose Luis Mata-Cedillo, an illegal alien from Mexico convicted of cocaine trafficking and firearms offenses. He had previously been deported twice and reentered the country illegally multiple times.

item.title: ICE Arrests Illegal Aliens Convicted of Murder, Sexual Assault, and Kidnapping
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested several illegal aliens with prior convictions for murder, sexual assault, kidnapping, and drug trafficking. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there will be no sanctuary for illegal aliens under the Trump Administration.

item.title: DHS Says ICE Deported Convicted Gang Members, Murderers and Other Criminal Aliens Last Week
item.description: DHS issued a press release on October 8 stating that ICE deported several criminal illegal aliens last week, including individuals convicted of murder, sexual assault, robbery and DUI. The release names about ten individuals and details their criminal histories and nationalities.

item.title: CBP Proposes Changes to Low-Value Shipment Customs Entry Rules, Not Immigration-Related
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has proposed a rule modifying filing requirements for informal customs entries of goods valued at $2,500 or less, including a new electronic entry type for mail shipments. This is a customs and trade rulemaking and does not concern visas, green cards, or citizenship.

item.title: DHS Proposes New Fees of Up to $70,000 for F-1 Student OPT Work Authorization
item.description: DHS has issued a proposed rule to impose new fees on F-1 nonimmigrant students participating in Optional Practical Training (OPT). The rule, which is not yet final, would set a $70,000 fee for initial OPT and a $30,000 fee for subsequent OPT.

item.title: DHS Spotlights Illegal Alien Arrests and Convictions in San Antonio, Texas
item.description: On October 7, 2026, DHS released a statement highlighting illegal aliens arrested by ICE or convicted of crimes in San Antonio, Texas, including cases involving child sex trafficking, drug trafficking and theft. The release frames these cases as examples of ongoing enforcement efforts following what DHS described as prior border policy failures.

item.title: ICE Arrests Nigerian National Working on PA Congressional Campaign After Indecent Exposure Case
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested Chimaobim Adedayo Igbojekwe, a Nigerian national unlawfully present in the United States, after he pleaded guilty to disorderly conduct in Pennsylvania. He had been working as a canvasser for a congressional campaign.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Criminal Illegal Aliens Convicted of Child Sex Abuse, Drug Trafficking
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested several criminal illegal aliens with convictions including sexual conduct against a child, sexual abuse of an animal, and drug trafficking. The release lists five individuals, their countries of origin, convictions, and arrest locations across several U.S. states.

item.title: DHS Proposes $70,000 Initial and $30,000 Subsequent Fees for F-1 OPT
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has filed a proposed rule that would create new fees for Optional Practical Training (OPT) under the F-1 student visa program. The rule would require a $70,000 fee for initial OPT and a $30,000 fee for any subsequent OPT period, applying to each F-1 student at a SEVP-certified institution.

item.title: Italian National Indicted for Voting in 2024 Election and Lying on Naturalization Form
item.description: USCIS assisted in the federal investigation leading to the indictment of Andrea Catanese, a 60-year-old Italian national, for voting while not a U.S. citizen and making false statements on his naturalization application. If convicted on all counts, he faces up to 10 years in federal prison.

item.title: DHS Statement on Stabbing of Off-Duty NYPD Detective by Two Illegal Aliens, Suspects At-Large
item.description: DHS issued a statement after two men in the country illegally were accused of stabbing an off-duty NYPD detective during an attempted robbery in the Bronx on October 2. ICE identified the suspects as Dominican Republic nationals with prior criminal histories and said both had previously been released by local authorities despite ICE detainer requests.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Illegal Aliens Convicted of Child Abuse, Money Laundering, Drug Trafficking
item.description: DHS announced on October 6, 2026 that ICE arrested several illegal aliens with prior convictions, including lewd acts with a child, money laundering, and drug trafficking. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said ICE will continue to find and remove individuals who entered the country illegally and broke the law.

item.title: ICE Lodges Detainer for Illegal Alien Charged with Sexually Assaulting a Minor in Tennessee
item.description: DHS announced that ICE lodged a detainer for a 22-year-old Honduran national charged with statutory rape and sexual exploitation of a minor in Nashville, Tennessee. The individual had illegally entered the United States through Texas in March 2021 and was released into the country after being arrested by Border Patrol.

item.title: ICE Reports Weekend Arrests of Convicted Murderers, Child Sex Offenders and Drug Traffickers
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced the arrest of multiple illegal aliens with prior convictions for murder, child rape, sexual assault and drug trafficking over the weekend. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the operation reflects the administration's public safety priorities despite a reported sharp rise in assaults on ICE officers.

item.title: DHS Secretary Mullin Observes Deportation Flight to El Salvador
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin observed a deportation flight departing Alexandria, Louisiana for El Salvador, which removed 100 illegal aliens, including individuals convicted of murder, sexual assault and driving while intoxicated. DHS stated the mission reflects ongoing mass deportation efforts.

item.title: DHS Highlights Cases of Undocumented Immigrants Arrested or Convicted in Nebraska
item.description: DHS issued a press release naming five undocumented immigrants arrested or convicted of crimes in Nebraska, including allegations of terrorism plotting, gang membership and sexual assault. The release includes a statement from DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and does not announce any new policy or rule.

item.title: DHS Waives Certain Laws to Speed Border Wall Construction in New Mexico
item.description: The Secretary of Homeland Security has determined, under section 102 of IIRIRA, that certain federal and state legal requirements will be waived to allow expedited construction of border barriers and roads in a segment of New Mexico within the El Paso Sector. The determination took effect on October 2, 2026.

item.title: Former Syrian Prison Warden Sentenced to 60 Years for Torture and Immigration Fraud
item.description: Samir Ousman Alsheikh, a former warden of Syria's Adra Prison and provincial governor, was sentenced to 60 years in prison for torture and immigration fraud. USCIS assisted in the investigation that led to his conviction.

item.title: White House Sets FY2027 Refugee Ceiling at 17,500, Prioritizes South African Afrikaners
item.description: On September 25, 2026, the President issued Presidential Determination No. 2026-24, setting the Fiscal Year 2027 refugee admissions ceiling at up to 17,500 and directing that admissions be primarily allocated to Afrikaners from South Africa under Executive Order 14204. The determination was published in the Federal Register on October 2, 2026.

item.title: Federal Grand Jury Indicts Ten Noncitizens for Voter Fraud in Minnesota
item.description: On Sept. 24, a federal grand jury separately indicted ten noncitizens for voter fraud in Minnesota elections. The investigation was led by ICE Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS. All defendants have made their initial court appearances.

item.title: USCIS: Use Dates for Filing Chart for All Adjustment of Status Filings in October 2026
item.description: USCIS has designated the Dates for Filing chart in the October 2026 Department of State Visa Bulletin for both family-sponsored and employment-based adjustment of status applications. Applicants in categories that are current, or where the Final Action Dates chart cutoff is later, may still file under the Final Action Dates chart.

item.title: DHS Raises Two HR-1 Immigration Enforcement Fees to $5,300 for FY2027
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has issued its fiscal year 2027 inflation adjustment for two immigration enforcement fees created by HR-1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Both fees, which apply to aliens arrested after an in absentia removal order and to inadmissible aliens apprehended between ports of entry, rise from $5,130 to $5,300. DHS will begin assessing and collecting the new amounts on October 16, 2026.

item.title: DHS Sets FY 2027 Inflation Adjustments for Parole, I-94, ESTA and EVUS Fees
item.description: DHS has announced Fiscal Year 2027 inflation-adjusted amounts for certain immigration fees required by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (HR-1), including the parole fee, ESTA fee and EVUS enrollment fee. The new amounts take effect October 16, 2026. The Form I-94 fee at land border ports of entry will not change for FY 2027 due to the statutory rounding rule.

item.title: USCIS Announces FY2027 Inflation Adjustment to H.R. 1 Immigration Fees
item.description: USCIS has published the Fiscal Year 2027 inflation adjustment to immigration fees established under H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act). The adjustment reflects a 3.36 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) between July 2025 and July 2026. The new fees take effect for requests postmarked on or after October 16, 2026.

item.title: USCIS Finalizes EB-5 Fee Increases, Effective November 30, 2026
item.description: DHS and USCIS published a final rule adjusting fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program, codifying provisions of the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022. The rule takes effect November 30, 2026, and raises several Integrity Fund fees along with other EB-5 immigration benefit request fees. It responds to public comments on a proposed version of the rule published October 23, 2025.

item.title: USCIS Announces FY 2027 Inflation Adjustment for Certain H.R. 1 Immigration Fees
item.description: USCIS has published a Federal Register notice raising certain H.R. 1 immigration-related fees for fiscal year 2027 to account for inflation from July 2025 through July 2026. The new fees take effect on Oct. 16, 2026, and apply to requests postmarked on or after that date.

item.title: EOIR Announces FY2027 Inflation Adjustment to OBBBA Fees for Certain DHS Forms
item.description: The Department of Justice's Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) has issued a notice detailing FY2027 inflation adjustments to OBBBA fees for certain DHS forms filed in immigration court and before the Board of Immigration Appeals. The adjustments implement a final rule already published on August 21, 2026, and take effect October 1, 2026.

item.title: USCIS Helps Florida Charge 16 Noncitizens With Unlawful Voting
item.description: USCIS assisted a Florida investigation that led to charges against 16 noncitizens accused of registering to vote by falsely claiming U.S. citizenship and then voting. Four additional individuals were charged with voting while on felony probation. USCIS confirmed the alien status of the individuals involved, according to the Florida Attorney General's Office.

item.title: USCIS to Adjust EB-5 Fees to Cover Program Costs and Boost Integrity Measures
item.description: USCIS announced it is updating fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program so that fees fully recover the cost of running the program, meet statutory processing time goals, and support integrity measures such as audits and site visits. The change finalizes a proposed rule published by DHS in October 2025. The source does not specify exact new fee amounts.

item.title: Cuban National Convicted in International Alien Smuggling and Money Laundering Case
item.description: USCIS supported an investigation that led to the conviction of Lazaro Alain Cabrera-Rodriguez, a Cuban national, for conspiring to run an international alien smuggling organization and launder its proceeds. The organization charged between $1,500 and $40,000 per smuggled migrant and used fraudulent ESTA applications and false claims of European citizenship.

item.title: Romanian National Pleads Guilty to Conspiring in Marriage Fraud Scheme
item.description: Antonia-Beatrice Mircea, a Romanian citizen, admitted to conspiring with a U.S. citizen to enter a sham marriage to obtain lawful permanent residence. USCIS assisted the federal investigation, announced by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of New Jersey.
